page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: Alpha taxonomy is classification based only on
morphological characters — the external form of
the root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit and seed.
It is the earliest stage: plants are described,
named and grouped from what can be seen.
steps.why: The word "only" is the whole definition. Alpha taxonomy is defined by what it leaves out as much as by what it uses.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the word "only", which turns the definition into any taxonomy.
Calling it the final stage. Alpha is the first stage.
steps.memory_tip: Alpha is the first Greek letter and the first look, the outside only.
steps.margin_note: Two lines. The word "only morphological" must appear.

steps.label: What it does not use

lines.text: Alpha = morphology only; omega = all data

lines: and serology are NOT used at the alpha stage.
steps.why: Naming the contrast proves you know the term belongs to a series, and it is the quickest way to show the boundary of the definition.
common_mistakes: Mixing the two up and saying alpha uses all data.
Writing that alpha taxonomy is wrong. It is a stage, not an error.
steps.memory_tip: Alpha first, omega last: alpha uses the outside only, omega uses everything.
steps.margin_note: One boxed contrast line is enough for this mark.

insider_note: Alpha and omega come as a pair in this chapter. Learn the contrast once and both two-mark questions are answered.
